derivations.claim: Work first over $S=\mathbb Z[p_1,\ldots,p_N]$ with universal monic $p$. Its full splitting ring is $\mathbb Z[X_1,\ldots,X_N]$, finite free over $S$ on the successive monic Artin basis. The block-invariant ring $L_r$ is a direct summand of this module: multiply by the staircase in each of the two blocks and apply the two longest divided differences; the resulting $L_r$-linear map fixes $L_r$ by [F2]. Thus $L_r$ is finite projective over $S$. The same argument with blocks of sizes $r,1,N-r-1$ applies to $B_r$. Monic division gives its displayed free bases over $L_r$ and $L_{r+1}$. Consequently $P=B_{r-1}\otimes_{L_{r-1}}B_{r-1}$ and $V=B_r\otimes_{L_{r+1}}B_r$, with their shifts restored later, are finite projective over $S$: choose a relative power basis in one tensor factor and use projectivity of the other. They inject into their generic-root scalar extensions. The coefficient pairings are perfect because their power-basis Gram matrices have unit antidiagonal and zero entries below it. For a monic $f$, their Casimir is $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$, since coefficient extraction in $X$ gives $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$. This proves both triangles by dual-basis contraction and defines all four maps integrally before any localization.

Localize the universal root ring at all root differences. Vertices are now indexed by subsets $J$ of roots of size $r$. Put $c(u)=\prod_{w\in J}(u-w)$ and $b(u)=\prod_{z\notin J}(u-z)$. A path in $P$ removes $w\in J$ and then adds a root; a path in $V$ adds $z\notin J$ and then removes a root. Paths with different initial and final subsets are the single common swap path $J\to J-w+z$. Paths with equal endpoints are the $P_w$ and $V_z$ components. The coefficient trace on a monic root extension is $f\mapsto\sum_\xi f(\xi)/f_0'(\xi)$; this is polynomial Lagrange interpolation followed by top-coefficient extraction. Therefore $\eta_z=c(z)$, $\varepsilon'_z=1/b'(z)$, $\eta'_w=b(w)$ and $\varepsilon_w=1/c'(w)$. Units and caps have zero components on swap paths because their source or target is the identity bimodule.

We verify the claimed Morita normalization independently. Let $I_r:L_r\to S$ be the positive parabolic trace: over generic roots it is $I_r(f)=\sum_{|J|=r}f(J)/\prod_{w\in J,z\notin J}(w-z)$. This is an integral polynomial map: factor the full monic splitting-tower trace through the two block traces; equivalently apply the normalized parabolic longest divided difference. It is perfect. Indeed, on the block Artin basis the perfect full pairing is the direct sum of copies of the $I_r$ pairing composed with the invertible block Gram matrix; its inverse shows each copy is invertible. The actual nil-Hecke quotient is this matrix algebra: in the power basis of the monic $X_1$ extension, the first column of multiplication by the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$ contains all remainder coefficients, and every matrix entry belongs to their ideal. Matrix units therefore identify the two-sided ideal $(p(X_1))$ with that coefficient ideal. Monic division identifies its vanishing quotient with $L_r$. $$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. Single curls instead have literal-dot sum $a+b=-1$.

For a symmetrizable datum and distinguished color $i$, take a dominant integral framing $\lambda_i\geq0$ and
$$p(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij},\qquad t_{ij}=[u^{-a_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,y)\in D^\times.$$
This realizes every $r\geq0$, including both signs of $h$, with zero modules past $N$. Appending a color $j$ root uses the quotient and multiplication by $Q_{ij}$, and the mixed mate pair constructed with the first unit/first cap and second unit/second cap has composites $t_{ij}$ in **both** orders. This identifies the actual mixed mates in the distinguished-$i$ flag model. Compatibility with adjunctions for a second distinguished color is a separate assembly question.

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls
$$L_\mu=(H\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G)(H\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H)(G\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H),$$
where $L_\mu$ has input $\mu$ and $R_\mu$ input $\mu-\alpha_i$, with $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=h$. Their formulas are
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+j=-h}x^a\mathsf H_j,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+j=h}x^aA_j.$$
All indices in these sums are nonnegative. Mating the two matrix-completeness equations gives the two opposite-crossing cancellation equations with literal-dot sum $a+b+c=-2$: the $HG$ boundary uses $A_{b+h+1}$, and the $GH$ boundary uses $\mathsf H_{b-h+1}$. Single curls instead have literal-dot sum $a+b=-1$.

For a symmetrizable datum and distinguished color $i$, take a dominant integral framing $\lambda_i\geq0$ and
$$p(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij},\qquad t_{ij}=[u^{-a_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,y)\in D^\times.$$
This realizes every $r\geq0$, including both signs of $h$, with zero modules past $N$. Appending a color $j$ root uses the quotient and multiplication by $Q_{ij}$, and the mixed mate pair constructed with the first unit/first cap and second unit/second cap has composites $t_{ij}$ in **both** orders. This identifies the actual mixed mates in the distinguished-$i$ flag model. Compatibility with adjunctions for a second distinguished color is a separate assembly question.

Under the nil-Hecke matrix equivalence the first cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm new}$ and the normalized relative second cap is exactly $\tau_{\rm old}$: the normalization is $\widehat\varepsilon_r=(-1)^{N+1}\varepsilon_r$ for the ordered-residue relative form defined in the proof. No formal diagram-model realization, categorical commutator, cyclotomic Frobenius theorem, or one-dimensional Hom hypothesis is a premise. Every assertion is an integral polynomial identity, hence survives arbitrary monic specialization. Grading is asserted only when the coefficients are homogeneous in their natural degrees.
replacement.facts_and_assumptions_exact:
**Given:** A monic polynomial $p$, the actual flag bimodules and coefficient adjunctions above, the native nil-Hecke crossing, and, for the mixed-color clauses, a weighted-homogeneous KLR datum and a dominant framing.

[F1] In [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], the native divided difference is $(1-s)/(X-Y)$, and the source crossing is $\kappa=-\tau$ for every color pair; the dot and crossing degrees are those of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].

[F2] The Artin polynomial module, its perfect longest-divided-difference pairing and its matrix units are proved in the matrix calculation of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]].
replacement.proof_exact:
**Proof technique:** constructive: evaluate the actual cups, crossings and caps on universal root paths, identify both diagonal matrices with polynomial interpolation and monic division, and descend their identities from the generic roots to integral flag bimodules.

1.1 Work first over $S=\mathbb Z[p_1,\ldots,p_N]$ with universal monic $p$. Its full splitting ring is $\mathbb Z[X_1,\ldots,X_N]$, finite free over $S$ on the successive monic Artin basis. The block-invariant ring $L_r$ is a direct summand of this module: multiply by the staircase in each of the two blocks and apply the two longest divided differences; the resulting $L_r$-linear map fixes $L_r$ by [F2]. Thus $L_r$ is finite projective over $S$. The same argument with blocks of sizes $r,1,N-r-1$ applies to $B_r$. Monic division gives its displayed free bases over $L_r$ and $L_{r+1}$. Consequently $P=B_{r-1}\otimes_{L_{r-1}}B_{r-1}$ and $V=B_r\otimes_{L_{r+1}}B_r$, with their shifts restored later, are finite projective over $S$: choose a relative power basis in one tensor factor and use projectivity of the other. They inject into their generic-root scalar extensions. The coefficient pairings are perfect because their power-basis Gram matrices have unit antidiagonal and zero entries below it. For a monic $f$, their Casimir is $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$, since coefficient extraction in $X$ gives $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$. This proves both triangles by dual-basis contraction and defines all four maps integrally before any localization. [F2, construct, algebra]

2.1 Localize the universal root ring at all root differences. Vertices are now indexed by subsets $J$ of roots of size $r$. Put $c(u)=\prod_{w\in J}(u-w)$ and $b(u)=\prod_{z\notin J}(u-z)$. A path in $P$ removes $w\in J$ and then adds a root; a path in $V$ adds $z\notin J$ and then removes a root. Paths with different initial and final subsets are the single common swap path $J\to J-w+z$. Paths with equal endpoints are the $P_w$ and $V_z$ components. The coefficient trace on a monic root extension is $f\mapsto\sum_\xi f(\xi)/f_0'(\xi)$; this is polynomial Lagrange interpolation followed by top-coefficient extraction. Therefore $\eta_z=c(z)$, $\varepsilon'_z=1/b'(z)$, $\eta'_w=b(w)$ and $\varepsilon_w=1/c'(w)$. Units and caps have zero components on swap paths because their source or target is the identity bimodule. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 We verify the claimed Morita normalization independently. Let $I_r:L_r\to S$ be the positive parabolic trace: over generic roots it is $I_r(f)=\sum_{|J|=r}f(J)/\prod_{w\in J,z\notin J}(w-z)$. This is an integral polynomial map: factor the full monic splitting-tower trace through the two block traces; equivalently apply the normalized parabolic longest divided difference. It is perfect. Indeed, on the block Artin basis the perfect full pairing is the direct sum of copies of the $I_r$ pairing composed with the invertible block Gram matrix; its inverse shows each copy is invertible. The actual nil-Hecke quotient is this matrix algebra: in the power basis of the monic $X_1$ extension, the first column of multiplication by the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$ contains all remainder coefficients, and every matrix entry belongs to their ideal. Matrix units therefore identify the two-sided ideal $(p(X_1))$ with that coefficient ideal. Monic division identifies its vanishing quotient with $L_r$. Put $V_r$ for the resulting first-block Artin module, $M_r=\operatorname{End}_{L_r}(V_r)=\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ and $t_r=s_rI_r\operatorname{Tr}_r,\qquad s_r=(-1)^{r(N-r)+r(r-1)/2}.$ The sign is also the ordered-residue sign: in $(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}(\Delta_rX_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}_r(-)/\prod_ap(X_a))$, group ordered tuples by subsets; their alternating determinant contributes $\Delta_r^2$, while the internal derivative factors contribute $(-1)^{r(r-1)/2}\Delta_r^2$. Cancellation gives exactly $t_r$, without $1/r!$. Define the bilinear relative cap by $t_r\varepsilon_r=t_{r+1}$ using the perfect $t_r$ pairing. The constant-vector matrix idempotent identifies the induction corner with $B_r$ and its dual corner with $g\mapsto[v\mapsto\tau_{\rm new}(gv)]$; matrix evaluation is therefore precisely $\tau_{\rm new}$. On the rank-one operator $v\mapsto f\tau_{\rm new}(gv)$, its matrix trace is $\tau_{\rm new}(gf)$. [step 1.1, F2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Compute the displayed mates on these path components, using the actual crossing $(1-s)/(X-Y)$. On the equal-endpoint components the result is $(-T)_{z,w}=\frac{c(z)}{c'(w)(z-w)},\qquad S_{w,z}=\frac{b(w)}{b'(z)(w-z)}.$ Here the first expression is the cup factor $c(z)$, the no-switch divided-difference entry $1/(w-z)$ on the ordered additions $(w,z)$ in $T$, and the first-cap factor $1/c'(w)$. For $S$, the twofold first mate reverses the addition path. Its no-switch coefficient on ordered removals $(z,w)$ is $1/(w-z)$; its switch coefficient, evaluated on the output removal order $(z,w)$, is $1/(z-w)$. To check this transposition, the composed first-cap weight on the additions $(z,w)$ over a common subset $K$ is $1/[c_K(z)c_K(w)(w-z)]$, and the exchanged order has its negative. Their ratio changes the sign of the off-diagonal transposed crossing and leaves the diagonal coefficient unchanged. Thus the second cup in $S$ contributes $b(w)$, its no-switch entry is $1/(w-z)$, and the second cap contributes $1/b'(z)$. This is a computation of the defined mate, not a definition of $S$ by the inverse matrix. On a swap path $J\to J'=J-w+z$, the first contraction in $T$ instead has numerator $c_{J'}(w)=(w-z)c_{J-w}(w)$ and denominator $(w-z)c'_J(w)=(w-z)c_{J-w}(w)$, together with the native minus sign; thus $T=-1$. For the switched second contraction, the complementary factor at $J'=J-w+z$ is $b_{J'}(z)=(z-w)b_{J^c-\{z\}}(z)$; its second-cap denominator is $b'_J(z)=b_{J^c-\{z\}}(z)$, and its switched upward crossing contributes $1/(z-w)$. Therefore $S=1$ on this path. One may check the transposition without notation for diagrams: replace each root delta-vector by its dual vector multiplied by the derivative of its monic root polynomial, apply $(1-s)/(X-Y)$, and contract; the two derivative multipliers are exactly the four factors just displayed. Hence $-ST=-TS=1$ on every swap component. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 Write $n=N-r=\deg b$. On the equal-endpoint components $U=-T$ sends values $(f_w)$ to the values at $z\notin J$ of the unique polynomial $F(u)$ of degree $<r$ with $F(w)=f_w$, because its matrix is $c(z)/(c'(w)(z-w))$. Similarly $S$ sends $(g_z)$ to the values at $w\in J$ of the unique polynomial $G(u)$ of degree $<n$ with $G(z)=g_z$. If $h=n-r\geq0$, then $SU=1$. Monic division writes $G=cq+v$ uniquely with $\deg q<h$, $\deg v<r$. Thus $US$ is evaluation of $v$ and $Cq$ is evaluation of $cq$, proving $US+CR=1$ once the rows $R$ extract the coefficients of $q$. To identify these rows, expand $\frac{G(u)}{b(u)}=\sum_z\frac{g_z}{b'(z)(u-z)},\qquad \frac{G(u)}{c(u)}=u^hA(u^{-1})\frac{G(u)}{b(u)}.$ The coefficient of $u^k$ in the polynomial part of the second expansion is precisely $\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\sum_z g_zz^a/b'(z)$, which is the prescribed $R_k$. Therefore $RU=0$, $SC=0$, $RC=1$ and $US+CR=1$, as well as $SU=1$. These prove all five positive-branch equations, including the prescribed inverse rather than an unspecified polynomial section. At $h=0$ monic division has no quotient, and $U,S$ are mutually inverse. [step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 If $h<0$, interchange $c$ and $b$ in the preceding division. Interpolate the $P$ values by $F$ of degree $<r$, and write $F=bq+v$ with $\deg q<-h$, $\deg v<n$. Now $US=1$ on $V$, $SU$ is evaluation of $v$ on $P$, and $C^-q$ is evaluation of $bq$. Expanding $F/b=u^{-h}\mathsf H(u^{-1})F/c$ identifies the coefficient rows of $q$ with $R^-_k$ exactly. Hence $UC^-=0$, $R^-S=0$, $R^-C^-=1$ and $SU+C^-R^-=1$. With $U=-T$ these are the five asserted negative-branch equations. This proof includes $r=0$, $r=N$ and $N=0$ by empty interpolation sets; beyond the factor range every module is zero. All equations were identities between integral maps on the projective modules in step 1.1, so injection into the generic-root extension proves them over $S$. Base change gives them over every $D$; no root difference is inverted in the resulting maps. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The single-curl contraction uses one crossing instead of the two in $US$ or $SU$. On the reversed flag removing $w$, cup, the no-switch upward crossing and cap contract to $-\sum_z c(z)/[b'(z)(w-z)]$, using the weights of step 2.1 and the upward crossing entries of step 3.1. This is the polynomial part of $c(u)/b(u)$ evaluated at $w$: explicitly, subtracting $\sum_z c(z)/(b'(z)(u-z))$ from $c(u)/b(u)$ removes all its simple poles and leaves its monic-division quotient. On the reversed flag removing $z$ at the adjacent input $r+1$, the other-handed contraction is $\sum_w b(w)/[c'(w)(z-w)]$. Since $b(z)=0$, this is minus the polynomial part of $b(u)/c(u)$ evaluated at $z$. Since $c/b=u^{-h}\mathsf H(u^{-1})$ and $b/c=u^hA(u^{-1})$, these are the two stated finite sums. The first has degree $-2dh$ at input $\mu$; the second has degree $2dh$ at input $\mu-\alpha_i$. The two-turn contractions are respectively $d(1-h)+d(1-h)-2d$ and $d(1+h)+d(1+h)-2d$, verifying the input-weight distinction. At $h=0$ they give $+1$ and $-1$. Mating the completeness identities in steps 4.1-5.1 uses only the already proved triangles, and expands $C_kR_k$ or $C^-_kR^-_k$ as the finite triple convolution. In the first case $a+j+c=h-1$ and literal clockwise dots are $b=-h-1+j$, so $a+b+c=-2$; in the other case $a+j+c=-h-1$ and counterclockwise dots are $b=h-1+j$, with the same total. These are actual opposite-crossing boundary maps, with the bubble in outside region $\mu$. The same conversion on the single-curl sums gives $a+b=-1$. Integral descent is as in step 5.1. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 For $f\in B_r$, comparison of root denominators gives $I_r\tau_{\rm old}(f)=(-1)^rI_{r+1}\tau_{\rm new}(f)$: the two denominators agree except for the $r$ factors $w-z$ versus $z-w$. Moreover $s_{r+1}/s_r=(-1)^{N-r-1}$, hence $(-1)^{N+1}s_{r+1}/s_r=(-1)^r$. Testing the relative cap on the rank-one operators of step 2.2, also after multiplication by every element of $L_r$, now identifies $\widehat\varepsilon_r=(-1)^{N+1}\varepsilon_r$ with $\tau_{\rm old}$ by perfection. The corresponding relative unit is its dual-power-basis Casimir, so the identification includes the unit and both triangles, not only a trace value on dots. All denominator comparisons are comparisons of already integral polynomial maps between projective modules, and descend exactly as in step 5.1. [step 1.1, step 2.2, algebra]

7.1 For the mixed clauses write $p'=pq$, $q=Q_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$ monic of degree $A=-a_{ij}$, and $U_r=\prod_{a=1}^rQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$. Multiplication by $U_r$ defines the matrix-quotient map from the old factor block to the new one; cancellation in the ordered-residue polynomial expression gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$. Testing the relative cap against $U_ra$ and using its bilinearity and the perfect old trace gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q_{ij}(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^At_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z).$ The test also proves independence of the lift. The normalized caps of step 6.2 cancel $(-1)^A$, because $N$ changes to $N+A$. Thus the actual flag cap constant is $t_{ij}$. For $r=0$ this is simply top-coefficient extraction $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$; arbitrary polynomial reduction gives the same equality. Dual-basis contraction proves the companion cup equation. [step 2.2, step 6.2, algebra]

8.1 More explicitly, fix the mixed boundaries $G_jH_i$ and $H_iG_j$ and source crossings $\kappa=-\tau$. The handed pair is $a=(H_iG_j\varepsilon)(H_i\kappa_{ij}H_i)(\eta G_jH_i),\qquad b=(\varepsilon'G_jH_i)(H_i\kappa_{ji}H_i)(H_iG_j\eta').$ The intermediate words are $H_iG_iG_jH_i$ and $H_iG_jG_iH_i$. The quotient/switch gives $a$ the canonical underlying flag identification; the multiplication-by-$Q$ switch and the normalized coefficient cap in step 7.1 give $b$ its scalar $t_{ij}$. Consequently $ba=t_{ij}1_{G_jH_i}$ and $ab=t_{ij}1_{H_iG_j}$. Native crossings multiply both $a,b$ by $-1$ and preserve these products. Thus the inverse mixed crossing is obtained by dividing its companion mate by $t_{ij}$. The same calculation for a separately distinguished color $j$ gives $t_{ji}$ for its own pair; identifying both partial actions inside a coherent full action is not a consequence of these two scalar tests alone. Dots commute with the quotient and multiplication maps. With $i$ last, the downward shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$ gives both downward crossings degree $-b_{ij}$; the basic mixed flag identification has shift $-b_{ij}$, canceled by the input-weight change in $H_i(m)=E_i^{\rm basic}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. The normalized mixed maps are therefore degree zero. [F1, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 The first unit and second cap have degree $d(1-h)$, and the first cap and second unit degree $d(1+h)$, by coefficient extraction of $z^r$ and $z^{N-r-1}$ with the displayed shifts. Hence $T,S$ have degree zero, $C_k$ has degree $d(1-h+2k)$ and $R_k$ its negative, while $C^-_k$ has degree $d(1+h+2k)$ and $R^-_k$ its negative. Steps 4.1-5.1 establish both actual matrix inverses, step 6.1 the typed curls and cancellations, and steps 2.2, 6.2, 7.1 and 8.1 the normalized cap transport and mixed orientations. Universal construction followed by base change includes every dominant framing, every permitted color and every weight in its factor range, with no characteristic restriction or choice principle. Nonhomogeneous monic specializations preserve the maps and equations as ungraded identities. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 6.2, step 8.1, discharge-construct: actual polynomial flag maps] ∎

citations.quote:
For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Four oriented same-color equations.** The following notation specifies
actual local diagrams, all with color $i$. The two-crossing equations have
common outside weight $\mu$; the single curls have the adjacent region
weights specified individually below.
Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
(two bottom endpoints and no top endpoints), whose tangent at its peak
points left or right, respectively. Their bottom arrows, from left to
right, are $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$ and
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$. Let $U_L,U_R$ be the cup valley
(two top endpoints and no bottom endpoints), whose tangent at its trough
points left or right; their top arrows are
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$ and $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$.
An exponent on $C$ or $U$ counts dots on its open arc. Let $B_{\mathrm{ccw}}^b$
and $B_{\mathrm{cw}}^b$ be the counterclockwise and clockwise bubbles
with literal dot count $b$, located to the right of the cap/cup in the outside
region of weight $\mu$. Their negative dot counts are exactly the fake
bubbles defined by the coefficient conventions above, not zero by convention.
Write $\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$ and
$\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$ for the first unit and second counit,
and $\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the second unit and first counit. Let $\tau^{HH}$ be the twofold
adjunction mate of the native equal-color downward crossing. Define
$$L_\mu=(H_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G_i)(H_i\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H_i)(G_i\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H_i).$$
The first formula starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu$; the second
starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu-\alpha_i$. Thus both units and
counits in $L_\mu$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$, while those in $R_\mu$ have
degree $d_i(1+h)$. The crossing degree $-2d_i$ makes their degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ respectively. Products in these formulas apply the
rightmost map first, with adjacent weights determined by composition.
Geometrically $L_\mu$ is an upward-strand curl with its loop bulging LEFT and
its left-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. This is an endomorphism of
$H_i$ at input $\mu$, and its bubble on the right-hand side is in the
left region $\mu$. Let $R_\mu$ be the upward-strand curl with its loop
bulging RIGHT and its right-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. Its left
region is $\mu-\alpha_i$, so it is an endomorphism of $H_i$ at input
$\mu-\alpha_i$, and its bubble is in the right region $\mu$.
Both have one native crossing and the two extremal turns of the loop.
Let $D_{\downarrow\uparrow}$ and $D_{\uparrow\downarrow}$ be the two
opposite crossing mates composed in the two orders on their indicated
straight boundaries, with common outside region $\mu$. Impose
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^b,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^b,$$
$$D_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-1_{\downarrow\uparrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_L^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^bU_R^c,$$
$$D_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-1_{\uparrow\downarrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_R^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^bU_L^c.$$
Composition in the last two displays is top-to-bottom: $U$ first, then
the outside bubble, then $C$. The single-curl equations are upward-strand
endomorphism equations; their cup/cap forms are their specified adjunction
mates, not cap drawings with unspecified endpoint arrows. In every sum,
$a,c$ on open strands are nonnegative. The clockwise bubble with literal
$b$ dots is the $A_\mu$ coefficient of index $b+h+1$, and the
counterclockwise bubble is the $\mathsf H_\mu$ coefficient of index
$b-h+1$, where $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Coefficients of negative index
are zero and the index-zero coefficient is one. The nonnegative coefficient
and open-dot indices make each sum finite. The opposite-crossing equations
have degree zero: their correction degrees are
$2d_i(1-h)+2d_i(a+b+c+h+1)=0$ and
$2d_i(1+h)+2d_i(a+b+c-h+1)=0$. The two curls have degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ at their respective, different input weights.

The native single-crossing signs follow from $\kappa=-\tau$; two-crossing
signs are unchanged. The literal triple-dot sum is $-2$, not the compact
$-1$ printed in Webster's Figure 2: in the full positive-weight equation,
coefficient indices satisfy $f_1+f_2+f_3=h-1$ and the bubble has literal
count $b=-h-1+f_2$, giving $a+b+c=-2$; the negative-weight equation uses
$g_1+g_2+g_3=-h-1$ and $b=h-1+g_2$, giving the same value. Reflection
exchanges the two bubble orientations and preserves region weights. The
single-curl coefficient sums instead have total $h$ or $-h$, yielding

curls are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ on their specified shifted input

first cancellation is $0=-1_k+1_k$, with no degree or vacuum contradiction.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$

$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard

$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not

assigned to it.

used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

derivations.claim: Actual cap and index. Apply the ordinary first unit to $e(\eta)$ and decorate its appended strand with $m$ dots; the resulting element is $e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$. The canonical first-adjoint transport preserves that unit by [F1]. Its actual second counit consequently evaluates this element as the transported diagram $\varepsilon'_\mu x^m\eta_\mu$, with $\mu=\Lambda-\gamma$. This is the counterclockwise bubble of [F2], hence $e(\eta)\mathsf H_{\eta,m-h_i+1}$. This calculation identifies the constructed $T_i^\gamma$ itself; it does not replace it by a chosen coefficient functional. Negative indices give zero, and no sign or weight shift is omitted: the literal-dot index is $m-h_i+1$, and its degree is $2d_i(m-h_i+1)=2d_im+\deg T_i^\gamma$.

Slide through the prefix. Starting with the vacuum value in [F2], slide the bubble through the chronological letters of $\eta$. Each coefficient computation is finite because every reversed monic factor has constant coefficient one. The resulting series is $\mathsf H_\eta(t)=\prod_{a:\eta_a=i}(1-x_at)^2/(a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)\prod_{a:\eta_a\ne i}q_{i\eta_a}^{\mathrm{rev}}(x_a,t))$. The numerator has degree $2\#\{a:\eta_a=i\}$ in $z$, the denominator has degree $\lambda_i+\sum_{a:\eta_a\ne i}(-a_{i\eta_a})$, and their difference is $-h_i$. Therefore $R_i^\eta(z)=z^{-h_i}\mathsf H_\eta(z^{-1})$. Extracting coefficient $z^{-1}$ from $z^mR_i^\eta(z)$ extracts precisely index $m-h_i+1$ from $\mathsf H_\eta$. Combined with step 1.1 this proves the actual terminal-dot formula, without restriction on the sign of $h_i$.

Centrality and old algebra factors. For an equal-color adjacent pair in $\eta$, the two factors of $\mathsf H_\eta$ are symmetric in their dot variables, so each coefficient commutes with its crossing by [F3]. For a distinct-color pair, swapping the color-variable pairs sends the coefficient in the $\eta$ summand to the coefficient in the swapped-word summand; its crossing has precisely that dot-permutation relation with no correction. Thus the finite sum of these coefficients over the words commutes with every crossing, every dot and every idempotent, which generate $A$. They are central. Appended terminal dots commute with all old generators. For any $b\in e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$, [F1] consequently evaluates $\iota_i(b)e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$ as $b\,e(\eta)[z^{-1}]z^mR_i^\eta(z)$. By linearity this identifies the actual cap on every polynomial terminal with arbitrary old algebra coefficients.

First actual quadratic contraction. Put the $i$ dot $u$ on the appended prefix $\eta i$. Its actual terminal-$j$ formula of step 2.1 uses $R_j^{\eta i}(v)=t_{ji}R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ji}(v,u)$. In this identity the inverse is expanded at infinity in $v$ and has polynomial coefficients in $u$ and the old dots. Apply step 3.1 termwise to the polynomial $Q_{ij}(u,v)g(u,v)$: its old coefficients lie in the append image of $A[u]$. Since $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the denominator cancels in the Laurent series before taking the coefficient. The actual inner cap therefore gives $t_{ji}[v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)$. This is a polynomial in $u$ with old algebra coefficients: $g$ has finitely many powers of $u,v$, and only finitely many series coefficients contribute to $v^{-1}$. Apply the actual outer $i$ cap by step 3.1. The result is $t_{ji}[u^{-1}][v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)R_i^\eta(u)$.

Second contraction and common map. Interchange $i,j$ and keep the variables labeled by color. Now the inner $i$ cap uses $R_i^{\eta j}(u)=t_{ij}R_i^\eta(u)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$, giving $t_{ij}[v^{-1}][u^{-1}]g(u,v)R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)$ after the outer $j$ cap. Following the quadratic cancellation, each series depends on only its own terminal variable and the old commuting dots. Their coefficients commute with one another. On the finite polynomial $g$, both extractions use finitely many coefficients and therefore commute. The result of step 4.1 and this result are respectively $t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ and $t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ in the same old algebra corner. This is an equality of actual cap compositions, with an explicit common residual map before any prefix closure; no common finite flag coefficient ring or symmetric trace was assumed.

Quotients and boundaries. Every input is evaluated by the actual append homomorphisms and actual quotient caps; two polynomial inputs with the same terminal quadratic image give the same cap value. Because $t_{ij},t_{ji}$ are nonzero, the identities also show that $\mathcal D_\eta$ vanishes on each kernel of the corresponding quadratic evaluation. No injectivity of the append homomorphisms is required. If an old or terminal corner is zero, the same equations are identities of zero actual maps. For the empty prefix $R_i(z)=1/a_i(z)$, giving ordinary monic top-coefficient extraction; $a_i=1$ and negative bubble indices are included by step 1.1. Every inverse-series coefficient is obtained by finite recursion from a unit constant term. Thus arbitrary monic field specialization preserves the argument, with grading forgotten, and there is no separability, characteristic-zero, finite-type or choice hypothesis. In the standard homogeneous case the degree asserted in step 1.1 agrees with [F1], and the two composite cap degrees agree in the two orders by $d_ia_{ij}=d_ja_{ji}$. The two-return contraction is proved; no conclusion about other terminal matching patterns is used or needed.

For the standard first-strand cyclotomic quotient of a real symmetrizable KLR
datum over any degree-zero field and every homogeneous (Q1)–(Q4) parameter
family, put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$,
$e=e(\beta,i)$, $X=Be$, $Y=eB$,
$h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $t=2d_i(1-h)$.
There are explicit, compatible homogeneous maps
$$T_i:eBe\longrightarrow A,\qquad \deg T_i=t,$$
and finite homogeneous tensors
$$C_i=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes_A y_\alpha\in X\otimes_A Y,\qquad \deg x_\alpha+\deg y_\alpha=-t,$$
such that $T_i$ is an $A$-bimodule map, $bC_i=C_ib$ for every $b\in B$, and
$$x=\sum_\alpha x_\alpha T_i(y_\alpha x),\qquad y=\sum_\alpha T_i(yx_\alpha)y_\alpha.$$
In particular $X\{t\}\cong\operatorname{HOM}_A(Y,A)$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules,
where Hom is left-$A$-linear, the left $B$-action is precomposition with
right multiplication on $Y$, and the right $A$-action is multiplication on
values. The second unit is $b\mapsto bC_i$ and the second counit is
$y\otimes_B x\mapsto T_i(yx)$, giving
$E_i\{t\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded modules. They are obtained by
finite normal-form/cap transport, not by assuming an actual Frobenius trace.
Dots and same-color crossing mates have the native cyclic normalization.
Each specified distinguished-$i$ different-color sideways pair has both
composites $t_{ij}$ times the identity. The separately distinguished-$j$
construction has both composites $t_{ji}$ times the identity. These are
different partial actions, not two different scalar values for the two
orders of one pair; their full word-closure comparison is not inferred here.
Arbitrary monic field specializations have the same ungraded construction,
with grading shifts forgotten. No finite-type, characteristic-zero,
geometric-global-basis or symmetric-trace premise is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Four oriented same-color equations.** The following notation specifies
actual local diagrams, all with color $i$. The two-crossing equations have
common outside weight $\mu$; the single curls have the adjacent region
weights specified individually below.
Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
(two bottom endpoints and no top endpoints), whose tangent at its peak
points left or right, respectively. Their bottom arrows, from left to
right, are $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$ and
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$. Let $U_L,U_R$ be the cup valley
(two top endpoints and no bottom endpoints), whose tangent at its trough
points left or right; their top arrows are
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$ and $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$.
An exponent on $C$ or $U$ counts dots on its open arc. Let $B_{\mathrm{ccw}}^b$
and $B_{\mathrm{cw}}^b$ be the counterclockwise and clockwise bubbles
with literal dot count $b$, located to the right of the cap/cup in the outside
region of weight $\mu$. Their negative dot counts are exactly the fake
bubbles defined by the coefficient conventions above, not zero by convention.
Write $\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$ and
$\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$ for the first unit and second counit,
and $\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the second unit and first counit. Let $\tau^{HH}$ be the twofold
adjunction mate of the native equal-color downward crossing. Define
$$L_\mu=(H_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G_i)(H_i\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H_i)(G_i\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H_i).$$
The first formula starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu$; the second
starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu-\alpha_i$. Thus both units and
counits in $L_\mu$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$, while those in $R_\mu$ have
degree $d_i(1+h)$. The crossing degree $-2d_i$ makes their degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ respectively. Products in these formulas apply the

Geometrically $L_\mu$ is an upward-strand curl with its loop bulging LEFT and
its left-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. This is an endomorphism of
$H_i$ at input $\mu$, and its bubble on the right-hand side is in the
left region $\mu$. Let $R_\mu$ be the upward-strand curl with its loop
bulging RIGHT and its right-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. Its left
region is $\mu-\alpha_i$, so it is an endomorphism of $H_i$ at input
$\mu-\alpha_i$, and its bubble is in the right region $\mu$.
Both have one native crossing and the two extremal turns of the loop.
Let $D_{\downarrow\uparrow}$ and $D_{\uparrow\downarrow}$ be the two
opposite crossing mates composed in the two orders on their indicated
straight boundaries, with common outside region $\mu$. Impose
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^b,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^b,$$
$$D_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-1_{\downarrow\uparrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_L^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^bU_R^c,$$
$$D_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-1_{\uparrow\downarrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_R^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^bU_L^c.$$
Composition in the last two displays is top-to-bottom: $U$ first, then
the outside bubble, then $C$. The single-curl equations are upward-strand
endomorphism equations; their cup/cap forms are their specified adjunction
mates, not cap drawings with unspecified endpoint arrows. In every sum,
$a,c$ on open strands are nonnegative. The clockwise bubble with literal
$b$ dots is the $A_\mu$ coefficient of index $b+h+1$, and the
counterclockwise bubble is the $\mathsf H_\mu$ coefficient of index
$b-h+1$, where $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Coefficients of negative index
are zero and the index-zero coefficient is one. The nonnegative coefficient
and open-dot indices make each sum finite. The opposite-crossing equations
have degree zero: their correction degrees are
$2d_i(1-h)+2d_i(a+b+c+h+1)=0$ and
$2d_i(1+h)+2d_i(a+b+c-h+1)=0$. The two curls have degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ at their respective, different input weights.

The native single-crossing signs follow from $\kappa=-\tau$; two-crossing

presentation by generators and homogeneous equations, and every sl(2) infinite
family appearing in the matrix and bubble clauses is a finite coefficient
recursion from a constant coefficient $1$.

below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

derivations.claim: Actual cap and index. Apply the ordinary first unit to $e(\eta)$ and decorate its appended strand with $m$ dots; the resulting element is $e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$. The canonical first-adjoint transport preserves that unit by [F1]. Its actual second counit consequently evaluates this element as the transported diagram $\varepsilon'_\mu x^m\eta_\mu$, with $\mu=\Lambda-\gamma$. This is the counterclockwise bubble of [F2], hence $e(\eta)\mathsf H_{\eta,m-h_i+1}$. This calculation identifies the constructed $T_i^\gamma$ itself; it does not replace it by a chosen coefficient functional. Negative indices give zero, and no sign or weight shift is omitted: the literal-dot index is $m-h_i+1$, and its degree is $2d_i(m-h_i+1)=2d_im+\deg T_i^\gamma$.

Slide through the prefix. Starting with the vacuum value in [F2], slide the bubble through the chronological letters of $\eta$. Each coefficient computation is finite because every reversed monic factor has constant coefficient one. The resulting series is $\mathsf H_\eta(t)=\prod_{a:\eta_a=i}(1-x_at)^2/(a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)\prod_{a:\eta_a\ne i}q_{i\eta_a}^{\mathrm{rev}}(x_a,t))$. The numerator has degree $2\#\{a:\eta_a=i\}$ in $z$, the denominator has degree $\lambda_i+\sum_{a:\eta_a\ne i}(-a_{i\eta_a})$, and their difference is $-h_i$. Therefore $R_i^\eta(z)=z^{-h_i}\mathsf H_\eta(z^{-1})$. Extracting coefficient $z^{-1}$ from $z^mR_i^\eta(z)$ extracts precisely index $m-h_i+1$ from $\mathsf H_\eta$. Combined with step 1.1 this proves the actual terminal-dot formula, without restriction on the sign of $h_i$.

Centrality and old algebra factors. For an equal-color adjacent pair in $\eta$, the two factors of $\mathsf H_\eta$ are symmetric in their dot variables, so each coefficient commutes with its crossing by [F3]. For a distinct-color pair, swapping the color-variable pairs sends the coefficient in the $\eta$ summand to the coefficient in the swapped-word summand; its crossing has precisely that dot-permutation relation with no correction. Thus the finite sum of these coefficients over the words commutes with every crossing, every dot and every idempotent, which generate $A$. They are central. Appended terminal dots commute with all old generators. For any $b\in e(\eta)Ae(\eta)$, [F1] consequently evaluates $\iota_i(b)e(\eta i)x_{n+1}^m$ as $b\,e(\eta)[z^{-1}]z^mR_i^\eta(z)$. By linearity this identifies the actual cap on every polynomial terminal with arbitrary old algebra coefficients.

First actual quadratic contraction. Put the $i$ dot $u$ on the appended prefix $\eta i$. Its actual terminal-$j$ formula of step 2.1 uses $R_j^{\eta i}(v)=t_{ji}R_j^\eta(v)/Q_{ji}(v,u)$. In this identity the inverse is expanded at infinity in $v$ and has polynomial coefficients in $u$ and the old dots. Apply step 3.1 termwise to the polynomial $Q_{ij}(u,v)g(u,v)$: its old coefficients lie in the append image of $A[u]$. Since $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, the denominator cancels in the Laurent series before taking the coefficient. The actual inner cap therefore gives $t_{ji}[v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)$. This is a polynomial in $u$ with old algebra coefficients: $g$ has finitely many powers of $u,v$, and only finitely many series coefficients contribute to $v^{-1}$. Apply the actual outer $i$ cap by step 3.1. The result is $t_{ji}[u^{-1}][v^{-1}]g(u,v)R_j^\eta(v)R_i^\eta(u)$.

Second contraction and common map. Interchange $i,j$ and keep the variables labeled by color. Now the inner $i$ cap uses $R_i^{\eta j}(u)=t_{ij}R_i^\eta(u)/Q_{ij}(u,v)$, giving $t_{ij}[v^{-1}][u^{-1}]g(u,v)R_i^\eta(u)R_j^\eta(v)$ after the outer $j$ cap. Following the quadratic cancellation, each series depends on only its own terminal variable and the old commuting dots. Their coefficients commute with one another. On the finite polynomial $g$, both extractions use finitely many coefficients and therefore commute. The result of step 4.1 and this result are respectively $t_{ji}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ and $t_{ij}\mathcal D_\eta(g)$ in the same old algebra corner. This is an equality of actual cap compositions, with an explicit common residual map before any prefix closure; no common finite flag coefficient ring or symmetric trace was assumed.

Quotients and boundaries. Every input is evaluated by the actual append homomorphisms and actual quotient caps; two polynomial inputs with the same terminal quadratic image give the same cap value. Because $t_{ij},t_{ji}$ are nonzero, the identities also show that $\mathcal D_\eta$ vanishes on each kernel of the corresponding quadratic evaluation. No injectivity of the append homomorphisms is required. If an old or terminal corner is zero, the same equations are identities of zero actual maps. For the empty prefix $R_i(z)=1/a_i(z)$, giving ordinary monic top-coefficient extraction; $a_i=1$ and negative bubble indices are included by step 1.1. Every inverse-series coefficient is obtained by finite recursion from a unit constant term. Thus arbitrary monic field specialization preserves the argument, with grading forgotten, and there is no separability, characteristic-zero, finite-type or choice hypothesis. In the standard homogeneous case the degree asserted in step 1.1 agrees with [F1], and the two composite cap degrees agree in the two orders by $d_ia_{ij}=d_ja_{ji}$. The two-return contraction is proved; no conclusion about other terminal matching patterns is used or needed.

oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$

$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
